analysis: The two units are CHANGELOG.md head-text excerpts (lines 266-790) and are documentation only. The patch shows the changed head range is 11-138, which is the new v0.10.1 candidate section. The supplied excerpts at lines 266 and later are mostly unchanged historical v0.10.0 and earlier notes, so no executable code, authorization logic, crypto or configuration changed in the visible text. I examined the security-relevant statements for contradictions with the threat model. T-041 (prefix cache): the notes say prefix reuse is partitioned by the authenticated cache scope, the SSD prefix store defaults on for the pinned GLM identity with the DARKBLOOM_PREFIX_CACHE=0 opt-out, and the debug-only cache key file exists in DEBUG builds only and is not in release builds. The SSD cache default TTL and storage claims are not changed in the visible text, and the 30-minute TTL and the salt scoping are not weakened. Release and staging pipeline notes (lines 669-685) say prod stays tag-gated, the staging lane is off by default, and the installer signature requirement is relaxed for -dev. and -staging. pre-release versions only. That is a rollout and trust-policy item for the platform, not a code regression visible here. It touches the provider artifact and qualification contract (A-011, A-017, T-054), and the changed relaxation of install.sh itself is not in the supplied evidence. Integration should check scripts/install.sh to confirm the relaxation cannot be reached by a production version string. The upgrade note about a coordinator requiring darkbloom-platform#411 for logprobs is an external contract that I cannot verify here. The unseen portion of the patch (lines 11-138) and the actual code changes in other files remain unreviewed, so the overall review has coverage limits. No concrete security regression is supported by these units.
